BregSurv for Claude Desktop — v1.0.0

This extension lets you run survival-analysis models from the BregSurv R package directly inside Claude Desktop. Describe your data and your question in natural language; Claude picks the appropriate Cox PH or nested case-control model, calls the corresponding R function on your machine, and explains the results.

Your data never leaves your computer. The extension passes only file paths to R; raw data is read locally and only the resulting summaries (coefficients, cross-validation scores, plots) are returned to Claude.

Note on the package name. This project was previously called SurvBregDiv. It is now BregSurv — the R package, the GitHub repository, and this extension. Older links redirect, but use the new name in install.packages / library calls.

Before you start — three points that account for almost all setup issues

  1. You must enable the extension after installing. New extensions appear in the Extensions list with the toggle in the OFF position. Installing only registers BregSurv with Claude Desktop; Claude will not see any of its tools until the toggle is switched ON. Details in the “Enable the extension” section below.

  2. If Claude proposes an analysis that does not match your request, force the wizard. Claude Desktop loads MCP tools lazily and may select a suboptimal tool on the first attempt. Saying “Please use the start_analysis wizard first” invokes the guided questionnaire, which deterministically routes to the correct model.

  3. Install the two prerequisites below before downloading the extension. R and the BregSurv R package are not bundled. Python, Node.js, and Conda are NOT required — Claude Desktop manages the Python runtime automatically.

What’s in v1.0.0

  • 33 MCP tools covering Cox proportional hazards and 1:m nested case-control designs, including low-dimensional, ridge, and elastic-net variants with cross-validation.
  • A guided wizard prompt (/bregsurv-start) that routes natural-language requests to the appropriate model.
  • Cross-platform support: a single platform-agnostic .mcpb bundle works on Windows, macOS (Intel and Apple Silicon), and Linux. The server auto-detects Rscript at standard install locations on each platform.
  • All computation runs locally through the user’s R installation; only tool names, arguments, and analysis results transit Anthropic’s API.

Prerequisites

1. R (>= version 4.0)

Check whether R is already installed:

  • Windows. Open the Start menu and type “R”. If you see “R x64 4.x.x” or “RStudio”, R is installed.
  • macOS. Open Terminal and run R --version. A version number indicates R is installed.
  • Linux. In a terminal, run R --version.

If R is missing or older than 4.0, install from https://cran.r-project.org/:

  • Windows: click “Download R for Windows” -> “base” -> run the installer with default settings.
  • macOS: click “Download R for macOS” -> select the .pkg matching your architecture (Apple Silicon for M1/M2/M3/M4 Macs, Intel for older models) -> run the installer.
  • Linux: follow the distribution-specific instructions on the CRAN page.

Verify the install. Open R and run R.version.string. The output should begin with R version 4.x.x.

2. The BregSurv R package

BregSurv is not yet on CRAN, so install it from GitHub. Open R and run:

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("UM-KevinHe/BregSurv")

The first install takes two to five minutes because it compiles C++ code. When the output ends with * DONE (BregSurv), the package is installed.

Verify the install. Run library(BregSurv). If R returns to the > prompt without error, the package is ready.

What you do NOT need to install

  • Python. Claude Desktop manages Python automatically for this extension via its bundled uv runtime.
  • Node.js or Conda / Anaconda.
  • A C++ compiler. The install will offer to install Rtools (Windows) or Xcode Command Line Tools (macOS) if needed.

Install the extension

  1. Download bregsurv-1.0.0.mcpb from the assets section below.
  2. Open Claude Desktop.
  3. Click the Settings icon, then Extensions in the sidebar.
  4. Click Advanced settings at the top of the Extensions page.
  5. Under Extension Developer, click Install Extension….
  6. Select the .mcpb file you downloaded.
  7. Claude Desktop will show an install dialog with a configuration form. The next section explains what to enter.

Installing by double-clicking the .mcpb file from a file manager is not documented to work. Use Settings -> Extensions.

Configure: provide the path to Rscript

The install dialog asks for the path to your Rscript executable. Rscript is installed alongside R; no additional installation is needed.

Typical locations:

  • Windows: C:\Program Files\R\R-4.x.x\bin\Rscript.exe (substitute your version, e.g. R-4.5.2).
  • macOS: /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Resources/bin/Rscript. Apple Silicon Macs may also have /opt/homebrew/bin/Rscript if R was installed via Homebrew; either works.
  • Linux: /usr/bin/Rscript or /usr/local/bin/Rscript.

To find the exact path:

  • Windows: open File Explorer at C:\Program Files\R\, choose the latest R-x.y.z folder, then bin\Rscript.exe.
  • macOS / Linux: open a terminal and run which Rscript. The output is the path to enter.

After confirming, click Install. Claude Desktop sets up the extension’s Python environment in the background; the first install takes between thirty seconds and a few minutes.

Enable the extension

When the install completes, Claude Desktop returns to the Extensions page with BregSurv in the list. The toggle on the right side of its row defaults to OFF (gray).

Click the toggle to switch it ON (blue/green). Claude Desktop then starts the extension’s server; a brief “starting…” indicator may appear. Once the toggle is steady, the extension is active.

If the toggle is left OFF, Claude will not see any of the BregSurv tools in a new chat.

Verify

  1. Open a new chat in Claude Desktop.
  2. Type: “Use BregSurv to help me start a survival analysis.”
  3. Claude should respond with the guided wizard’s first question about your data.

If Claude asks about your data file and runs analysis steps without error, the extension is working.

Troubleshooting

Claude does not see BregSurv after installation. The extension is installed but not enabled. Go to Settings -> Extensions, locate BregSurv, and switch the toggle to ON. Open a fresh chat — existing chats need to be reopened to see newly enabled tools.

“Rscript not found” or “Could not find R”. The configured Rscript path is incorrect. Open Settings -> Extensions -> BregSurv and re-enter the path using the locations listed in the Configure section. On Windows, ensure the path ends in Rscript.exe.

“There is no package called ‘BregSurv’”. The R package is not installed under the R version the extension is calling. Open the same R version pointed to by Rscript, then run:

remotes::install_github("UM-KevinHe/BregSurv")
library(BregSurv)

If multiple R versions are installed, ensure BregSurv is installed in the R version selected for the extension, not a different one.

“Package ‘jsonlite’ is not available” or a similar dependency error. Run in R:

install.packages("jsonlite")

jsonlite is the JSON bridge between Python and R; BregSurv’s other dependencies (survival, RcppArmadillo, etc.) install automatically with the package.

The extension runs the wrong tool. Claude Desktop loads MCP tools lazily. If the proposed analysis does not match your request, send: “Please use the start_analysis wizard first.” That forces the guided questionnaire, which deterministically selects the correct tool.

A cross-validation plot does not render inline. Send: “Please draw the cross-validation curve as an inline artifact.” Claude will render the plot using its built-in artifact tool.

Any other issue. Open an issue at https://github.com/UM-KevinHe/BregSurv/issues with the operating system version, R version (R.version.string), the exact error message, and the prompt that triggered it.

Privacy

  • Data files remain on your machine. The extension passes only a file path to R, which reads the file locally.
  • Analysis results (coefficients, cross-validation scores, plots) are returned to Claude so that Claude can explain them. These travel through Anthropic’s API as part of the normal conversation.
  • Tool names and arguments transit Anthropic’s API as part of standard MCP operation.
  • If your data file contains PHI or otherwise sensitive information, note that derived results (for example, “coefficient for variable Age = 0.31”) appear in Claude’s responses and are therefore logged. Plan accordingly.

The full privacy model is documented in the project README.

Uninstall

Settings -> Extensions -> BregSurv -> Uninstall. This removes the extension from Claude Desktop. R and the BregSurv R package remain installed on your system.
